title: Flow Regulator: Gradient Batch Shaper and Kernel Reconciliation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce p99 tail latency and unit cost in continuous batching by introducing a lightweight flow regulator that uses short-horizon arrival-rate gradients to adapt batch hold-time and negotiate kernel choices at admission time. The system should gracefully favor low-latency kernel paths for latency-sensitive small requests while allowing slightly longer hold-windows to improve throughput for bursty, long-sequence workloads.

Why now: We see recurring tail spikes on mixed workloads (small chat messages interleaved with long completions). Existing admission heuristics either bias for throughput (long hold-times) or latency (short hold-times) but do not adapt quickly to changing arrival gradients; kernel selection is currently static at admission and sometimes picks slow kernels for short bursts. This ticket experiments with combining an arrival-gradient-based shaper with a kernel-reconciliation step that can switch a batch to an alternate kernel if the measured batch shape drifts significantly before decode.

Scope: Design + spike + small pilot on a dedicated pool. Deliverables: design doc + RFC, Spike results (A/B data), implementation PR for flow regulator + kernel handoff protocol, and canary rollout plan with dashboarding and rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Flow regulator prototype integrated into admission path and can be toggled via runtime flag
p99 tail latency reduction >= 15% on mixed small+long workloads in pilot vs baseline
Overall per-token cost reduction >= 10% when enabled on throughput-heavy workloads (no customer-visible correctness regressions)
Kernel reconciliation must complete without request-level errors and fall back to original kernel on mismatch
Observability: per-request proto metadata emitted (chosen hold-time, arrival-gradient, kernel-choice, reconciled_flag)
Canary rollout plan and rollback automation documented in RFC
comments: 2026-02-24 - Maya Chen: Created ticket. Initial hypothesis: short-horizon arrival-rate derivative (dR/dt) is a strong signal for whether to tighten or relax hold-time. Plan spike to collect traces and compute signal-to-noise.

2026-03-02 - Ravi Kumar: Spike finished. Collected 48h of traces from dedicated-chat pool (mixed traffic). Implemented offline estimator; conservative heuristic (hold +/- 25ms per 10% gradient) reduces aggregation variance. See /docs/confluence/flow-regulator-spike-20260302

2026-03-04 - Priya Singh (SRE): Observed that kernel-change mid-batch increased mutex contention in kernel registry in the prototype; added low-contention fast path and optimistic kernel handoff with checksum to avoid CNF. Patch in PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4587

2026-03-07 - Design review (Ethan Park): Confirmed UX for operator flags and console instrumentation needed: per-route "flow_mode" toggle and histogram of reconcile events. Action: Add console widget and alert for reconcile-rate > 1%

2026-03-10 - Experiment run: A/B 10% traffic on dedicated pool for 72h. Early results posted to perf dashboard. Observed p99 improvement on long sequences and slight p95 regression for single-token requests under extreme microbursts. Investigating microburst hedging threshold.

2026-03-12 - Ravi Kumar: Implemented microburst hedging (fast-escape path) when gradient exceeds threshold for <=10ms holding window. Will push PR for code review. Next: finalize canary steps and add stress test in CI
experiment_results: A/B (10% traffic, 72h) on dedicated-chat-pool: p99 reduced from 420ms -> 345ms for long-seq (>512 tokens) workloads (~17.9% improvement)
Throughput cohort: average tokens/sec improved by 9.8% for batched long sequences due to better holding decisions
Small-request cohort (<=8 tokens): median latency unchanged (45ms) but p95 increased from 120ms -> 132ms in rare microburst windows; mitigations outlined
Cost: estimated 11% unit-cost reduction for throughput-heavy routes when flow regulator is enabled (based on sampled billing traces)

Add reconcile-rate alert and console widget (observability)
Run targeted stress tests with synthetic microbursts and long-seq mixes in CI (loadgen scenarios)
